verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack Fury and burst you with empowered W before level 6; you win every all-in from level 1-5 and again after your core spikes.

brief.thesis: Illaoi wins this matchup 56% over 1275 games because her E (Test of Spirit) punishes exactly the all-in pattern Renekton relies on: he dashes in with E (Slice and Dice) and swings away, but her spirit still echoes damage back onto him even as he disengages. The matchup is a Fury-economy fight — Renekton without 50+ Fury hits like a minion, but with it his Q and W both upgrade into real threats, so the lane hinges on whether you fight him empty or full.

theirWindow.what: His Q (Cull the Meek) and W (Ruthless Predator) both upgrade — W becomes a 3-hit, 1.5s stun that shreds shields, and Q's damage and heal both increase. Don't stand still and trade autos here; back off or force the fight before he tops off Fury.

yourWindow.when: His Fury is low (just recalled or poked, not all-in'd) or he's under level 6
yourWindow.what: Land E (Test of Spirit) first, then W (Harsh Lesson, 4s cooldown) to leap in and trigger your Tentacles. Even if he E's away after trading, the spirit you ripped out still echoes damage back to him, so you win trades he thinks he escaped.

boots.why: 73.8% pick rate at 56.3% win rate — the flat physical damage reduction directly softens his auto-reset Q poke and empowered W stun combo.

Second item in the same path — the proc adds a slow that helps you stick W (Harsh Lesson) onto him before he can E away.

runes.keystoneWhy: 56% win rate at 51.4% pick — the bonus health and sustained proc damage win the extended trades this matchup turns into once you land E (Test of Spirit).

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 56% of games at the highest win rate (57.4%) — Teleport lets you reset after E/W all-ins and still make side-lane plays once your core items spike.

playing.title: Track his Fury before engaging
playing.detail: Below 50 Fury his Q and W hit for minion-tier damage and W stuns for only 0.75s. Above 50, both abilities upgrade and his W stun doubles to 1.5s — all-in him empty, not full.

playing.title: E before every trade
playing.detail: Rip his spirit with E (Test of Spirit, 16/15/14/13/12s cooldown) before committing. The spirit echoes a percentage of damage back onto him even if he E's (Slice and Dice) away mid-fight.

playing.title: Respect level 6 dash-ins
playing.detail: Dominus grants bonus health and periodic Fury on top of his existing kit. Don't contest him in melee range right as he hits 6 without first checking his Fury bar.

playing.title: Use W to close, not just engage
playing.detail: W (Harsh Lesson) is a 4s cooldown leap that also triggers nearby Tentacles to swing. Chain it after E lands so the spirit echo and the Tentacle hits stack in the same trade.

playing.title: Hold Tentacle Smash for all-ins
playing.detail: Q (Tentacle Smash, 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown) increases Tentacle damage — pre-smash a Tentacle near your E target before you commit so the echo damage is maximized.

playing.title: Punish his E cooldown
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s on cooldown. After he dashes in and out once, he has no gap-closer or escape — this is your window to walk him down with W leaps.

playing.title: Save R for a trading window, not a reset
playing.detail: Leap of Faith (120/95/70/70/70s cooldown) spawns a Tentacle on hit and deals area damage. Use it to extend a fight you're already winning via E/W, not as a panic button.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoners reflect measured games on the current patch (OP.GG); the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice are our own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Rather than engaging in first, use your [E] when he uses his (E) to brawl. Even if Renekton deals his full combo and falls back with (E), deal damage to his spirit from [E] to fight back. However, Renekton has the upper hand after reaching level 6 and without proper items, so we advise not overreaching until then.
